```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(magrittr, include = "%<>%")
library(gtsummary)
library(dfmtbx)
```

```{r}
env_var <- "med_int_survey" # string variable containing RedCap API token

report_id <- 202713 # numeric variable containing the RedCap report id

# Skeleton to pull RedCAP data as raw, label, and headers
label <- pull_redcap_report(
  Sys.getenv(env_var),
  report_id,
  "label",
  "raw",
  "false"
)

raw <- pull_redcap_report(
  Sys.getenv(env_var),
  report_id,
  "raw",
  "raw",
  "false"
)

field_text <- pull_redcap_report(
  Sys.getenv(env_var),
  report_id,
  "raw",
  "label",
  "false"
)
```

```{r}
# Merge in numeric columns
column_order <- label %>% names()

numeric_columns <- raw %>%
  select(starts_with("conf"), starts_with("gender"), starts_with("race_eth"), -gender_desc)
  
numeric_col_names <- numeric_columns %>%
  names()
```

```{r}
data <- label %>%
  select(-(all_of(numeric_col_names))) %>%
  bind_cols(., numeric_columns) %>%
  select(all_of(column_order))
```

```{r}
# Harmonize the pre and post test column names
# Two possible ways of doing this. Use the redcap event and filter out the separate sections, then stack
# Could also possibly coalesce 4x

pre_conf <- data %>%
  filter(redcap_event_name == "Baseline") %>%
  select(record_id, redcap_event_name, conf_1, conf_2, conf_3, conf_4)

post_conf <- data %>%
  filter(redcap_event_name %in% c("Follow Up", "Follow Up 2") %>%
  select(record_id, redcap_event_name, conf_12, conf_22, conf_32, conf_42)

names(post_conf) <- c("record_id", "redcap_event_name", "conf_1", "conf_2", "conf_3", "conf_4")

conf <- bind_rows(pre_conf, post_conf)

data %<>%
  select(-starts_with("conf"))

data <- data %>% left_join(., conf, by = c("record_id", "redcap_event_name"))
```

```{r}
# Age
data %<>%
  mutate(age = as.numeric(age)) 

# Gender
# No on selected more than one gender
n_mt1_gen <- data %>%
  filter(redcap_event_name == "Baseline") %>%
  mutate(mt1_gen = rowSums(across(gender___1:gender___5), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(mt1_gen > 1) %>% 
  nrow()

# Create gender
data %<>%
  mutate(gender = ifelse(
    gender___1 == 1, "Female",
    ifelse(gender___2 == 1, "Male",
    ifelse(gender___3 == 1, "Non-binary", 
    ifelse(gender___4 == 1, "Prefer to self-describe",
    ifelse(gender___5 == 1, "Choose not to disclose", "Unknown"))))
  ))

# Create race/ethnicity
# One person selected more than one race
data %<>%
  mutate(mt1_race = rowSums(across(race_eth___1:race_eth___8), na.rm = TRUE))

n_mt1_race <- data %>%
  filter(mt1_race > 1) %>% 
  nrow()

data %<>%
  mutate(
    race_eth___1 = ifelse(race_eth___1 == 1, "Asian", NA),
    race_eth___2 = ifelse(race_eth___2 == 1, "Black", NA),
    race_eth___3 = ifelse(race_eth___3 == 1, "Indigenous North American", NA),
    race_eth___4 = ifelse(race_eth___4 == 1, "Indegenous other", NA),
    race_eth___5 = ifelse(race_eth___5 == 1, "Latino/a" , NA),
    race_eth___6 = ifelse(race_eth___6 == 1, "White/Caucasian", NA),
    race_eth___7 = ifelse(race_eth___7 == 1, "Prefer to self describe", NA),
    race_eth___8 = ifelse(race_eth___8 == 1, "Choose not to disclose", NA)
  ) %>%
  mutate(race_eth = coalesce(
    race_eth___1,
    race_eth___2,
    race_eth___3,
    race_eth___4,
    race_eth___5,
    race_eth___6,
    race_eth___7,
    race_eth___8
  )) %>%
  mutate(race_eth = ifelse(mt1_race > 1, "More than one race", race_eth))

# Reverse code the conf_* questions so that higher values represent
# better outcomes
data %<>%
  # select(starts_with("conf")) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("conf"), ~ (.x - 6) * -1))
```

  )

## Self-Confidence (Baseline vs Follow up)
```{r, warning = FALSE}
pre_post_data <- data %>%
  select(record_id, redcap_event_name, starts_with("conf"))

dvs <- c("conf_1", "conf_2", "conf_3", "conf_4")

# Model fitting function. This function is designed to utilize the map2() 
# function to loop through a set of data frame and dependent variable 
# pairs and fit a linear mixed effect model.
fit_model <- function(dv) {
  
  form <- as.formula(paste0(dv, " ~ redcap_event_name + (1 | record_id)"))

  # df %<>%
  #   mutate(timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("pre", "post")))

  # Linear mixed model for the tiib_pd data
  model <- lmerTest::lmer(form, data = pre_post_data)

  output_tbl <- broom.mixed::tidy(model, conf.int = FALSE)

  # extract the p-value from the comparison of post to pre
  p_val <- str_c("p = ", output_tbl %>% 
    filter(term %in% c("redcap_event_nameFollow Up", "redcap_event_nameFollow Up 2")) %>% 
    pull(p.value) %>%
    round(4))

  # emmeans
  emms_tbl <- emmeans::emmeans(model, ~ redcap_event_name) %>% as_tibble()

  # extract the means and se
  emms_tbl %<>%
    mutate(across(emmean:SE, ~ (round(.x, 2)))) %>%
    mutate(m_se = str_c(format(emmean, nsmall = 2), " (", SE, ")")) %>%
    mutate(p_val = c(" ", p_val) )

  # determine the y value for vjust
  emms_tbl %<>%
    mutate(y = emmean + SE)


  # plot
  plt <- emms_tbl %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=redcap_event_name, y=emmean)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = emmean - SE, ymax = emmean + SE), width = 0.10) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Confidence (mean +/- se)") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf(m_se)),
    hjust = -.25
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = p_val),
    hjust = -.25,
    vjust = 2
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(3, 5)) +
  theme_minimal()

  # Revert back to original emmeans table without the added variables for 
  # plotting 
  
  emms_tbl <- emmeans::emmeans(model, ~ redcap_event_name) %>% as_tibble()

  output <- list(
    output_tbl,
    emms_tbl,
    plt
  )
}

all_output <- map(dvs, fit_model)
```

```{r}
# Results summary for abstract
# Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine changes in confidence scores from pre- to post-training. Models included fixed effects for time (pre vs. post) and a random intercept for participant to account for repeated measurements. Model results indicated significant pre-to-post improvements in conf1 (b = 0.47, 95% CI [0.18, 0.75], p = 0.004), conf3 (b = 0.73, 95% CI [0.34, 1.12], p = 0.001), and conf4 (b = 0.60, 95% CI [0.25, 0.95], p = 0.003). There was no evidence of a pre-to-post change in conf2 (b = 0.07, 95% CI [-0.38, 0.51],  p = 0.751).
```
